raw.response:
Surya Namaskar, or Sun Salutation, is a sequence of 12 powerful yoga asanas best done early morning on an empty stomach [PROG_Y_001].

Ek complete round consists of two sets, starting with the right leg and then the left, with each posture coordinated with your breath [PROG_Y_001].

Anulom Vilom Pranayama mind ko calm karta hai aur stress ko relieve karta hai [PROG_P_001]. Ye body mein Tridoshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) ko balance karne mein madad karta hai [PROG_P_001]. Isse patience aur concentration bhi improve hota hai [PROG_P_001]. 

Isse subah (morning) breakfast se pehle karna sabse best hota hai, aur cold, cough, ya fever hone par iska abhyas na karein [PROG_P_001].

Ek healthy lifestyle ke liye balanced diet zaroori hai. Breakfast mein fried foods ki jagah poha, upma, ya idli lein [PROG_D_001]. Lunch mein 2 rotis, ek bowl dal, sabzi, aur salad shamil karein [PROG_D_001]. Dinner sabse halka hona chahiye, jiske liye khichdi ya dal ke sath vegetable stir-fry accha option hai [PROG_D_001]. 

Seasonal fruits aur vegetables khayein, processed sugar aur excessive salt se bachein [PROG_D_001]. Non-vegetarians ke liye fried ki jagah grilled chicken ya fish behtar hai, aur nuts and seeds se snacking karna cravings control karne mein madad karta hai [PROG_D_001]. Roz kam se kam 8-10 glasses paani (water) zaroor piyein [PROG_D_001].

Kapalbhati, or Skull Shining Breath, is an invigorating pranayama that cleanses the body through active, forceful exhalation and passive inhalation [PROG_P_002]. Sit comfortably with a straight spine, take a deep breath in, and exhale in short, powerful bursts while your stomach pumps inwards [PROG_P_002]. Start with a round of 20-30 pumps and do up to 3 rounds with breaks [PROG_P_002]. 

It stimulates the digestive system, improves metabolic rate, and aids in weight loss [PROG_P_002]. Perform it on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning [PROG_P_002]. Avoid this practice if you are pregnant, have high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, or epilepsy [PROG_P_002].

Trikonasana (Triangle Pose) is a foundational standing pose that stretches the entire body [PROG_Y_003]. To do it, stand with your feet wide apart, turn your right foot out 90 degrees, and your left foot in slightly [PROG_Y_003]. Exhale as you extend your torso to the right from the hips, place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor, and extend your left arm up [PROG_Y_003]. 

It stretches the hamstrings, hips, and spine while strengthening the legs and core, and improves digestion [PROG_Y_003]. Hold for 30-60 seconds, and avoid locking your knees [PROG_Y_003]. Avoid this pose if you have a headache, low blood pressure, or a neck injury [PROG_Y_003].

Garmi ke liye aap Sheetali Pranayama (Cooling Breath) kar sakte hain [PROG_P_004]. 

Comfortable baith kar apni tongue ko tube shape mein roll karke mouth se bahar nikalein [PROG_P_004]. Tube ke through slowly aur deeply inhale karein, fir tongue retract karke mouth close karein aur nostrils se slowly exhale karein [PROG_P_004]. Isko 5-10 times repeat karein [PROG_P_004]. 

Yeh body ko cool karta hai, mental aur emotional excitation reduce karta hai, aur hunger aur thirst ko control karne mein help karta hai [PROG_P_004]. 

Note: Low blood pressure ya asthma jaise respiratory issues wale logo ke liye yeh recommended nahi hai [PROG_P_004]. Clean environment mein practice karein [PROG_P_004].

Immunity badhane ke liye ek balanced diet zaroori hai [PROG_D_002]. Apni diet mein citrus fruits jaise amla, oranges, aur lemons shamil karein jo Vitamin C se rich hain [PROG_D_002]. Turmeric (haldi) mein curcumin hota hai, jo anti-inflammatory compound hai; ise milk ya curries mein add karein [PROG_D_002]. Ginger aur garlic bhi bahut faydemand hain [PROG_D_002]. Yogurt probiotics ka accha source hai gut health ke liye [PROG_D_002]. Green leafy vegetables jaise spinach (palak) antioxidants se packed hain, aur almonds Vitamin E ka great source hain [PROG_D_002].

Yogi Devvrat is a certified RYT 500 Yoga Alliance instructor with over 15 years of experience who began his journey in Rishikesh [PROG_I_001]. His teaching style blends classical Hatha yoga with modern Vinyasa flow, focusing on alignment and breath [PROG_I_001]. 

He specializes in therapeutic yoga, helping clients manage chronic pain and stress-related ailments, and often says, "Yoga ek yatra hai, manzil nahi" [PROG_I_001].

Millets are ancient grains that are gluten-free and rich in fiber, protein, and antioxidants [PROG_D_004]. They have a low glycemic index, making them suitable for diabetics, and their high fiber content keeps you full for longer to aid in weight management [PROG_D_004]. Specific varieties include Ragi (Finger Millet), which is a great source of calcium for bone health, Jowar (Sorghum), which is packed with iron and protein, and Bajra (Pearl Millet), which is rich in magnesium for heart health [PROG_D_004].

To relax, you can practice Shavasana (Corpse Pose). Lie flat on your back with your feet spread apart and arms by your sides, palms facing up. Close your eyes, let go of breath control, and release any tension (*thakaan*) [PROG_Y_004]. Spend at least 5-10 minutes in this pose to help reduce blood pressure, calm the nervous system, and combat insomnia while remaining aware and relaxed without falling asleep [PROG_Y_004]. 

Alternatively, you can try Balasana (Childs Pose) by kneeling on the floor, sitting back on your heels, and folding forward with your forehead on the floor [PROG_Y_005]. Hold this restorative pose for 30 seconds to a few minutes with deep, diaphragmatic breathing to calm the brain, alleviate stress, and relieve back and neck pain [PROG_Y_005].

Dia Malik is a certified clinical nutritionist with a Masters degree in Food and Nutrition [PROG_I_002]. She follows a no-deprivation approach and creates sustainable diet plans that fit your lifestyle and cultural eating habits [PROG_I_002]. You can book a one-on-one consultation with her to create a khaane ka plan (eating plan) that works for you [PROG_I_002]. She is available on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4 PM to 6 PM [PROG_I_002].

Hydration is crucial for overall health because water regulates body temperature, lubricates joints, and helps deliver nutrients to cells [PROG_D_003]. Dehydration can lead to headaches, fatigue, and poor concentration [PROG_D_003]. 

You should aim for 8-10 glasses of water per day, and drink more if you exercise or if it is a hot day [PROG_D_003]. Drinking water before meals aids in weight management, and it is also essential for kidney function and flushing out toxins [PROG_D_003]. You can infuse your water with lemon, cucumber, or mint leaves for better taste and added benefits [PROG_D_003].
